solutions.check: grid and clues read from the FT's printable PDF, its numbering matching the clue list; every fifteensquared answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Two-thirds of the way to mastering popular vernacular

indicators.note: loosely, 'the way to' asks for the remaining letters to be put into a fresh order
only six of the nine letters of the printed word are kept, the outer M, A and G being dropped

explanation.surface: A tip for getting most of the way to fluency in everyday speech.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Two-thirds of' keeps six of the nine letters of 'mastering', STERIN, and 'the way to' rearranges them. Strine is the jokey name for broad Australian speech, from 'Australian' said in that accent.
explanation.definitionFit: Strine is a humorous label for colloquial Australian English, the everyday slang of the country.

clue.text: *Takes great steps and pants

definitions.meaning: trousers, in British and Australian slang

explanation.definitionFit: The word is a verb for long purposeful walking and an informal noun for trousers.

clue.text: 17 wants money back? Get an expert in!

indicators.note: the expert is put inside the refund

parts.note: a rebate is a partial refund
a pro is a professional or expert

explanation.surface: A villain demands a refund and calls in a specialist.
explanation.walkthrough: 17 is WRONGDOER, which defines this answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A reprobate is an unprincipled person, a scoundrel or sinner.

clue.text: It points to embroidery without effort

indicators.note: the effort word is taken out of the sewing word

parts.note: needlework is sewing and embroidery
work is effort

explanation.surface: A sign points towards some easy embroidery.
explanation.definitionFit: A compass needle is the pointer that indicates north.

clue.text: Old transporter is a source of misery here!

parts.note: BR stands for British Rail, the former national railway
taken as written
a bane is a cause of great distress

explanation.surface: Someone grumbles that a former means of transport made this place miserable.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is just 'here': the Australian theme makes the city the place the clue speaks from, and its convict-colony origins make the misery apt.
explanation.definitionFit: The Australian theme sets the scene in the Queensland capital, so 'here' points to that city.

clue.text: *Racket partly wrong: right?

indicators.note: only part of the printed word is kept, its first and last two letters being dropped

explanation.surface: A racket played partly wrong: is that right?
explanation.walkthrough: A rort is an Australian scam or fiddle.
explanation.definitionFit: In Australian slang a rort is a fraudulent scheme or swindle.

clue.text: Practical baselines put out without American involvement

indicators.note: put out means disturbed, so the letters are thrown into a new order
the American letter is removed from the printed word

explanation.surface: Sensible lines are drawn up without US involvement.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Without American involvement' removes A from BASELINES, leaving BSELINES to rearrange.
explanation.definitionFit: Sensible means down-to-earth and practical in judgement.

clue.text: How a forward might hope to take a defender?

definitions.text: How a forward might hope to take a defender?

parts.words: How a forward might hope to take a defender?
parts.note: a forward hopes to get past a defender, and the idiom for being startled is built from that defender's position name

explanation.walkthrough: In football a defender is a 'back', and a forward wants to take one on; the idiom for being caught by surprise uses the same word.
explanation.definitionFit: Aback means by surprise, used in the phrase for being startled.

clue.text: One unearths former Cardinal's rule

parts.note: ex means former
Basil Hume was Cardinal Archbishop of Westminster

explanation.surface: Someone digs up the late Cardinal's regulation.
explanation.definitionFit: An exhumer is a person who digs up a buried body.

clue.text: *More mature, with a dash of paprika added — just fantastic

indicators.note: the letter is slipped into the word for 'more mature', so 'added' places it inside

parts.note: riper means more fully ripened or mature

indicators.note: a dash is a small amount, here the opening letter of the spice word

explanation.surface: A cook praises a riper dish improved by a sprinkle of paprika.
explanation.walkthrough: Ripper is Australian slang for something excellent.
explanation.definitionFit: In Australian slang a ripper is something excellent, so the word works as a superlative exclamation.

clue.text: Coarse stuff from untidy barn to grind

indicators.note: untidy means messed up, so the letters of the farm building are jumbled

parts.note: to mash is to crush or grind into a pulp

explanation.surface: Rough material is ground from a messy barn.
explanation.definitionFit: Bran mash is a coarse feed of bran and hot water given to horses, a rough mixture.

clue.text: *The best examples were picked off and soundly beaten

definitions.text: The best examples were picked off
definitions.meaning: skimmed off the best, as cream from milk

explanation.definitionFit: The verb covers skimming off the best part and, informally, trouncing an opponent.

clue.text: Limo losing back bumper in boring comedy

indicators.note: the shortened car word sits inside the word for boring

parts.note: dry means dull or boring

indicators.note: the car word drops its last letter, its rear end

parts.note: a Roller is slang for a Rolls-Royce, the classic luxury limousine

explanation.surface: A limousine with its rear bumper gone is a dull sort of joke.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Losing back bumper' trims ROLLER to ROLLE, which goes 'in' DRY.
explanation.definitionFit: Drollery is whimsical humour, a kind of quaint comic entertainment.

clue.text: *Genuine young couple, rich, no children, plummy at heart

parts.note: a DINK is a couple with a double income and no kids

indicators.note: the heart of a word is its central letters, here the middle two of six

explanation.surface: A well-off childless pair with posh accents are the real thing.
explanation.walkthrough: Dinkum (as in 'fair dinkum') is Australian for genuine.
explanation.definitionFit: Dinkum is Australian slang meaning honest, authentic or true.

clue.text: Old city in request for European body films

indicators.note: the old city sits inside the request

parts.note: a plea is an appeal or request
Ur is the ancient Mesopotamian city

explanation.surface: An ancient city features in an appeal for European documentaries.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Films' means thin membranes, not movies.
explanation.definitionFit: Pleurae are the thin membranes lining the chest and wrapping the lungs.

clue.text: *24 tinnies in a wooden hut? Piece of cake!

definitions.meaning: in Australia a carton of 24 cans of beer
a pioneer cabin built of split timber planks
a thick flat portion cut from a cake

explanation.walkthrough: Three meanings: two Australian (a case of 24 cans, a timber settler's hut) and a big portion of cake.
explanation.definitionFit: The word names an Australian beer carton, the timber of a bush hut and a thick portion of cake.

clue.text: Bloomer that attracts no attention

definitions.meaning: a flowering plant, something that blooms
a shy person left out at a dance or party

explanation.walkthrough: 'Bloomer' looks like a blunder, but it is simply something that flowers.
explanation.definitionFit: The name belongs both to a fragrant garden plant and to a shy person left unasked at a dance.

clue.text: One who rode badly?

parts.note: someone who did wrong, read as a jumble of the letters of rode

explanation.walkthrough: The letters of RODE disordered make DOER, a wrong 'doer' of rode; the plain meaning is a sinner.
explanation.definitionFit: A wrongdoer is a person who breaks the law or commits a misdeed.

clue.text: Spooner's friend to welcome pages of abuse!

indicators.note: the Reverend Spooner swapped the starts of words

parts.note: a mate is a friend
to hail is to greet or welcome

explanation.surface: A friend is greeted by poison-pen letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Hate mail is abusive or threatening correspondence.

clue.text: Failure to be revealed by whistle-blower at the end

definitions.text: Failure to be revealed by whistle-blower at the end

parts.words: Failure to be revealed by whistle-blower at the end
parts.note: the phrase means a scheme is exposed, and also what a referee's final whistle announces

explanation.walkthrough: 'Whistle-blower' suggests an informant exposing a plot, but it is also the referee ending a match.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom announces that a deception is discovered, and literally that play is over.

clue.text: Some pyjamas don't have close tops

indicators.note: the word for close is missing from the nightwear

parts.note: nightshirts are a kind of nightwear
nigh means near or close

explanation.surface: Some pyjamas lack snug-fitting upper halves.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Close tops' looks like a phrase about snug shirts; 'close' is NIGH and 'tops' is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: These short-sleeved casual shirts are worn on the upper body, garments called tops.

clue.text: *Sydney's crossing constructed at no charge

indicators.note: constructed means built, so the letters are assembled into a new arrangement

explanation.surface: Sydney's bridge was built without anyone paying for it.
explanation.walkthrough: The Sydney Harbour Bridge is nicknamed for its arched shape.
explanation.definitionFit: The Sydney Harbour Bridge is popularly called by this name because of its hooked arch.

clue.text: There it is! A four-in-hand

definitions.meaning: the huntsman's cry on sighting the fox
a fast coach drawn by four horses

explanation.definitionFit: It is the fox-hunting cry on sighting the quarry and the name of a four-horse coach.

clue.text: *Driven mad by drink when back on the river

indicators.note: back means the drink word is read in reverse

parts.note: port is a fortified wine
the Po is Italy's longest river

explanation.surface: Someone driven mad by drink when back on the river.
explanation.walkthrough: Troppo is Australian slang for crazy, as if from the tropical heat.
explanation.definitionFit: In Australian slang going troppo means going mad, supposedly from the tropical heat.

clue.text: See 20
*Greek letter to theologian you first uncovered

parts.note: nu is the 13th Greek letter
DD is a Doctor of Divinity

indicators.note: only the opening letter of the printed word

explanation.surface: A Greek character tells a theologian that you were first exposed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In the nuddy' is Australian and British slang for naked.
explanation.definitionFit: In the nuddy means naked, with nothing covering the body.

clue.text: Admiral Byng's final, out-of-tune, song

indicators.note: out of tune suggests letters jarring out of their order
the final letter of the admiral's name

explanation.surface: Admiral Byng's last song was badly sung.
explanation.walkthrough: John Byng was the admiral executed in 1757, adding to the surface's gloom.
explanation.definitionFit: A madrigal is a part-song for several unaccompanied voices.

clue.text: *Bought back one-piece swimming costumes

indicators.note: back means the word for bought is reversed

parts.note: got means acquired or bought
a single piece is singular, abbreviated S

explanation.surface: Someone buys back one-piece swimwear.
explanation.walkthrough: Togs is Australian for swimwear. Reading 'one-piece' as S for singular is the commenters' best guess.
explanation.definitionFit: In parts of Australia togs is the everyday word for swimwear.

clue.text: It gets heated if most of diary is wrong and timetable's gone west

indicators.note: being wrong means being out of order, so the letters are rearranged
all but the last letter of the printed word
in an across entry, going west means reading right to left

parts.note: a rota is a timetable of duties

explanation.surface: Someone gets hot under the collar over a muddled diary and a lost timetable.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Most of' leaves DIAR, rearranged ('is wrong') to RADI; 'gone west' turns ROTA into ATOR.
explanation.definitionFit: A radiator is a heating appliance that warms a room once hot water flows through it.

clue.text: See nothing in order inside, which is weird

indicators.note: the pieces go into the word for see

parts.note: to spy is to see or catch sight of
O looks like zero
OK means all right, in order

explanation.surface: Someone notices nothing amiss indoors, which is strange.
explanation.definitionFit: Spooky means eerie or unsettlingly strange.

clue.text: Good girl attracted to Bond, but he can see through it!

parts.note: James Bond is a fictional spy
a lass is a girl

explanation.surface: A nice girl falls for Bond, but he sees through her.
explanation.walkthrough: 'See through it' suggests seeing through a ruse, but it means looking through a telescope.
explanation.definitionFit: A spyglass is a small telescope, which a person looks through to see far off.

clue.text: *Cheers for four Oscars, the first two got in an hour

indicators.note: the first two letters are taken into the hour abbreviation

parts.note: HR is the abbreviation for hour
Oscar is O in the radio alphabet, so four Oscars give four Os
the other pair of the four Os

explanation.surface: A film collects four Oscars, the first two inside an hour, to applause.
explanation.walkthrough: 'The first two' says which pair of Os goes inside HR. Hooroo is Australian for goodbye.
explanation.definitionFit: Hooroo is an Australian farewell, like 'cheers' said when parting.
